catapult.title: Efficient 3-Step Workflow: predict → trace → simulate
catapult.principle: The fastest path to success is: (1) predict_first_contact to confirm the red ball hits the catapult arm, (2) trace_green_ball to verify the green ball reaches the basket region, (3) simulate_action only when trace confirms a viable trajectory. Skipping any step wastes iterations on failed simulations.
catapult.when_to_apply: Always — use this as the default action sequence for every attempt.
catapult.example: Seeds 18–20 all succeeded by following predict → trace → simulate with at most one radius adjustment.

catapult.title: Verify Green Ball Reaches Basket X Range via trace_green_ball
catapult.principle: Before running simulate_action, always call trace_green_ball to check whether the green ball's final resting position is within the basket x-range (~3.0–4.5) AND basket height (~y=-1.3 to -3.1). If the green ball lands short (x < 3.0), increase radius and retrace rather than simulate immediately.
catapult.when_to_apply: After every predict_first_contact that confirms arm contact, before simulate_action.
catapult.example: Seed 18: r=1.4 trace showed end=(2.62,-2.11) — short. r=1.5 trace showed end=(4.07,-1.38) — in range. Simulated r=1.5 → success.

catapult.title: Canonical Default Starting Placement: x=0.65, y=0.0, r=1.4
catapult.principle: When the pivot (gray_ball) is near x≈-0.93 to -1.2, placing the red ball at x=0.65, y=0.0 reliably strikes the catapult arm and launches the green ball rightward. r=1.4 is the correct starting radius — it may be sufficient or require upward adjustment depending on pivot position (see pivot-radius skill).
catapult.when_to_apply: As the first placement attempt whenever pivot x is in the range -0.93 to -1.2.
catapult.example: Seed 19 (pivot=-0.94): r=1.4 succeeded directly. Seeds 18, 20: r=1.4 was valid arm contact but needed radius increase.

catapult.title: Pivot Position Determines Required Launch Radius at x=0.65
catapult.principle: The further left the pivot (gray_ball) from x≈-0.94, the more radius is needed at x=0.65 to deliver sufficient impulse. Empirically: pivot≈-0.94 → r=1.4; pivot≈-1.04 → r=1.5; pivot≈-1.17 → r=1.6. Each ~0.1 leftward shift in pivot x requires roughly +0.1 in radius.
catapult.when_to_apply: After trace_green_ball confirms the green ball lands short of x=3.0 with r=1.4, or proactively when pivot x < -1.0.
catapult.example: Seed 20: pivot at x=-1.17, r=1.4 trace ended at x=2.33 (short), r=1.6 trace ended at x=3.81 → success.

catapult.title: Incremental Radius Tuning via trace_green_ball When Landing Short
catapult.principle: If trace_green_ball shows the green ball stops short of the basket (x < 3.0), increase the radius by 0.1–0.2 and retrace before simulating. The relationship between radius and launch distance is smooth at x=0.65 (no sharp cliff), so small increments reliably extend range by ~1.3–1.5 units per 0.1 radius increase.
catapult.when_to_apply: When trace_green_ball end x < 3.0 with canonical x=0.65 placement.

catapult.title: Adaptive X Fallback When Canonical Placement is Invalid
catapult.principle: If x=0.65, y=0.0, r=1.4 is invalid (object overlap), the scene geometry has shifted. Read the pivot x-position from describe_scene_geometry, then adjust the red ball's x to land on the right half of the catapult arm (roughly arm_center_x + 1.5 to arm_center_x + 2.0).
catapult.when_to_apply: When predict_first_contact returns placement_valid=False for the canonical position.
catapult.example: If the arm center shifts to x=-0.5, try x=1.0–1.5 instead of 0.65.

catapult.title: x>0.8 on Arm Dramatically Reduces or Reverses Green Ball Range
catapult.principle: Striking the catapult arm at x>0.8 (absolute) produces a contact point too close to or past the pivot, reducing mechanical advantage and launch distance. Keep the strike point at x≤0.75 to ensure the arm's right side goes down and the green ball launches upward-right.
catapult.when_to_apply: When considering x positions for the red ball drop; avoid x>0.8.
catapult.example: Canonical x=0.65 consistently hits the left portion of the arm for good leverage.

catapult.description: Agent persists with catapult strikes for many steps without verifying that the green ball ever reaches basket HEIGHT (y≈-1.3 to -3.1) during its arc — not just basket x-range.
catapult.why_it_happens: Agents fixate on x-range as the sole success criterion and miss that the green ball may overshoot vertically or arrive at the wrong height.
catapult.how_to_avoid: In trace_green_ball, check both end x (must be 3.0–4.5) AND end y (must be -1.3 to -3.1) before simulating.

catapult.description: Agent fine-tunes radius at a non-canonical x position when the catapult exhibits a sharp threshold cliff (tiny Δr causes swing from 'too short' to 'overshoot to floor').
catapult.why_it_happens: Agents assume linear radius-to-range relationship holds everywhere, but non-canonical x positions create unstable lever dynamics.
catapult.how_to_avoid: Return to x=0.65 for radius tuning; only adjust x when canonical placement is geometrically invalid.

catapult.description: Agent attempts placements in the basket/ledge region (x≈2.5–3.5, y≈-1.5 to -2.5) as deflectors that are consistently INVALID due to object overlap.
catapult.why_it_happens: Agents try to use the basket area as a deflection zone without checking that the basket and ledge already occupy that space.
catapult.how_to_avoid: Never place the red ball in x≈2.5–3.5, y≈-1.5 to -2.5; use predict_first_contact to verify placement_valid=True first.

catapult.description: Agent rapidly cycles through unrelated strategies (catapult → direct green hit → basket knockback → deflector) without converging on a viable mechanism.
catapult.why_it_happens: When the canonical placement fails once, agents abandon the approach instead of making targeted adjustments (radius tuning).
catapult.how_to_avoid: Exhaust radius adjustments (r=1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7) at x=0.65 before switching strategies; catapult mechanics are robust across scene variations.

catapult.description: Agent attempts to knock the blue ball leftward to meet the green ball without establishing where the green ball will be when blue arrives.
catapult.why_it_happens: Agents treat the blue ball as a movable target without modeling the green ball's landing position and timing.
catapult.how_to_avoid: Always establish the green ball's final position via trace_green_ball before attempting any blue ball manipulation strategy.
